title: Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising

issues.description: The whole comparison theory rests on one imported inequality: the covariance at arbitrary fields is at most the zero-field correlation (Ding-Song-Sun, Corollary 1.3). Here it is used with mixed-sign fields: after the shift by -A,-B, and from pins of both signs that were turned into fields. The paper states that the cited result covers arbitrary fields, and this matches the published statement as far as I recall it. I did not re-derive the cited result. This is a dependency to note, not a gap.
issues.evidence: "The Ding--Song--Sun inequality applies to this finite ferromagnetic graph with these arbitrary mixed-sign fields [Corollary~1.3]. It gives tanh K <= <sigma_I sigma_J>_0 = q_0."

main_claim: Finite-graph pointwise comparison: for a ferromagnetic Ising model with arbitrary common pins and fields, conditional likelihood ratios on I under two pinnings of J lie in [e^{-4 arctanh q0}, e^{4 arctanh q0}], where q0 is a zero-field FK connection probability on the pin-deleted graph with I and J contracted. This gives buffered and power-law patch comparisons at criticality. Main theorem (finite conditional resolution): for interface exploration across a fixed band, finitely many regular signed barriers approximate every good conditional target law in total variation (exceptional probability <= epsilon, error <= eta), uniformly over bounded observables, for all sufficiently fine meshes.
